data.name: Trinath
data.gender_notes: Trinath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Trinath is a name derived from Hindu mythology, signifying the belief in three principal gods - Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. It represents the idea of unified power and divine protection. The name Trinath carries the meaning “Three Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Trinath usually hope their child will grow to embody three gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Trinath is a sacred name that signifies devotion and faith towards the three principal gods of Hinduism - Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. It is believed to bestow the blessings of these deities and provide protection and strength.
data.etymology: Trinath belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Three Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Trinath total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who has three lords or masters. In Hinduism, this name is given to those who believe in three main deities: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.

in_hindi.name: त्रिनाथ
in_hindi.long_meaning: The master of the three purposes of human life: Dharma (duty), Artha (prosperity), and Kama (desire).

in_tamil.name: திரிநாத

data.cultural_impact: The name Trinath is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, emphasizing the importance of the tridevatas - the three principal gods - within the belief system. It is a testament to the richness and complexity of Hindu traditions, which recognize multiple gods and goddesses, each with distinct roles and attributes. In a multifaceted way, Trinath signifies the unity of various deities and the importance of respecting and honoring their diverse powers.
data.spiritual_significance: For individuals named Trinath or those who recite or use it as a mantra, it signifies the deep spiritual belief and acknowledgment of the three crucial aspects of divine protection - Creation (Brahma), Preservation (Vishnu), and Destruction (Shiva) - ensuring the cycle of life continues harmoniously. By carrying this name, being reminiscent of the ultimate power of the divine trinity, the individual is reminded of their spiritual connection and the interconnectedness of all things, guided by the virtues of creation, preservation, and destruction.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Trinath symbolizes the reverence for the three fundamental aspects of God - Brahma (creator), Vishnu (preserver), and Shiva (destroyer). This name signifies one's devotion and belief in the cyclical nature of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
